statement: A drip irrigation emitter releases $3$ milliliters of water every $10$ seconds. At this rate, how many liters of water does it release in one day? ($1$ liter $= 1{,}000$ milliliters)

choices.misconception: I counted a day as $60 \cdot 24 = 1{,}440$ seconds, but that is the number of minutes in a day, not seconds.
I read the rate as 3 milliliters every second, forgetting that it is every 10 seconds.
I found 25,920 milliliters correctly but forgot to divide by 1,000 to change milliliters to liters.

hints: Change the rate to milliliters per second first.
Multiply the milliliters per second by the number of seconds in a day, $60 \cdot 60 \cdot 24$, then convert to liters.
The rate is $0.3$ mL per second and a day has $86{,}400$ seconds, so the emitter releases $0.3 \cdot 86{,}400$ mL.

solutions.reliable: The rate is $3 \div 10 = 0.3$ milliliters per second. One day has $60 \cdot 60 \cdot 24 = 86{,}400$ seconds, so the emitter releases $0.3 \cdot 86{,}400 = 25{,}920$ milliliters. Dividing by $1{,}000$ gives $25.92$ liters. The idea: chain unit conversions so that each unit cancels, and check that the final unit matches the question.
solutions.elegant: Write it as one chain: $\dfrac{3\text{ mL}}{10\text{ s}} \cdot \dfrac{86{,}400\text{ s}}{1\text{ day}} \cdot \dfrac{1\text{ L}}{1{,}000\text{ mL}} = 25.92$ L per day.
